mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Cámara de Comercio in Colombia for the SAS; original authority in the shareholder's jurisdiction for passport or entity documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if originating in another Hague Convention member state) OR Consular Legalization for non-member state sources

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (Poder) for the incorporation representative or foreign shareholder appointing a Colombian legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the shareholder's country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-registration and ongoing screening against the U.S. OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Colombia's UIAF sanctions/laundering alert databases, and domestic judicial and police warning lists. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is required for Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) as defined under Colombian law and for any non-resident ownership from high-risk tax or sanction jurisdictions. The entity must implement and maintain a Spanish-language SARLAFT compliance manual, appoint a compliance officer, and document the shareholder/UBO screening process prior to filing with the Cámara de Comercio. Although this industry is classified Low_Risk_Standard, simplified due diligence does not eliminate reporting and disclosure duties under Decree 830 of 2021.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Decree 830 of 2021, Resolution 110-000035 of 2022, and External Circular 100-000005 of 2018 of the Superintendencia de Sociedades; Law 1121 of 2006 and Law 1621 of 2013; Commercial Code.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: UBO filings must be submitted to the Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUBF). Screening includes OFAC, UN, EU, and domestic Colombian lists; PEP and enhanced due diligence as required by External Circular 100-000005 of 2018; data is accessible only to designated authorities and not public.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Cámara de Comercio Online (RUES – Registro Único Empresarial, www.rues.org.co) and the local Cámara de Comercio, e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá (www.ccb.org.co) for name clearance (Certificado de Homogeneidad de Nombre)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be expressed in Latin script, typically in Spanish. A foreign-language name is acceptable if transliterated or written in Latin characters and clearly distinct from registered names. The suffix 'S.A.S.' must accompany the chosen name. Words must not be contrary to public policy, false, or contrary to good custom; the registration authority may request a Spanish description or explanatory translation where needed for registry clarity.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banco / Financiera / Capitalización / Fiduciaria (financial sector terms requiring prior Superintendencia Financiera authorization)
Nacional / Presidencia / Ministerio / Gobierno / Alcaldía / Departamento Administrativo (government or official-sounding tokens)
Palabras or symbols implying connection to the State or international bodies without authorized permission
Terms contrary to public health, morality, or public order
Well-known trademark or protected brand names without valid trademark permission
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon receiving a final rejection from the Cámara de Comercio, the applicant may file an administrative appeal (recurso de reposición / solicitud de reconsideración) within ten (10) business days from notification at the same Chamber, and alternatively file a hierarchical appeal (recurso de apelación) before the Superintendencia de Sociedades within the same term if the Chamber is the lower administrative body. The appeal must state the grounds for disregarding the negative clearance, include supporting trademark or ministerial authorizations, and propose modified suffix or alternative distinctive elements. In case of no response or adverse second decision, the applicant may pursue action before the Tribunal Administrativo (administrative court) under Ley 1437 of 2011, but in practice re-filing under a new name is faster and common.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is generally permissible for a low-risk SAS activity such as 3D art outsourcing, provided a registered address is established in the Chamber of Commerce jurisdiction where the company will receive legal notices and commercial mail. The law allows a SAS to operate with an administrative or virtual domicile, but the company must ensure the registered address is real, existing, and capable of receiving service of process; if using a virtual-office provider, the provider must be duly licensed and the address accepted by the Cámara de Comercio and DIAN. For ISIC 7490 (professional/business support services) and AAA game art outsourcing with no physical production plant, a virtual office is deemed acceptable and consistent with commercial substance if employees and books are verifiable elsewhere.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate for a low-risk virtual-office SAS; quantified probability of an unannounced on-site inspection in the first three years is estimated at 15–25%, increasing to 35–50% if later registration includes a physical commercial establishment, significant Colombian payroll, or high-volume cross-border payments requiring tax audit scrutiny. DIAN and Chamber of Commerce may verify the registered office during formal registry checks or targeted SME compliance reviews.

stage_1._internal_notes: No minimum capital requirement exists for Colombian SAS. The company may be incorporated with zero or nominal capital; however, bank and payment-processor onboarding will require declaration of initial equity, and a minimum working capital of at least USD 1,000 (approx. COP 4,000,000) is market practice to demonstrate bona fide commercial substance. All costs in this budget are pre-incorporation estimates exclusive of VAT and foreign-bank intermediary charges.
stage_1._schema_conformance_notes: The provided JSON Schema is generic object. All required fields from the specified structure are completed. Additional nested UBO detail is included under ubo_and_aml_profiling for completeness.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada), Articles 1-5, 10, 22; Código de Comercio Articles 110, 353-372; Decreto Único Reglamentario 1074 de 2015, Articles 2.2.2.38.1 et seq.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá (Chamber of Commerce) through the Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (Private Incorporation Document), authenticated by notary or filed directly at the Chamber of Commerce
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum capital under Article 4, Ley 1258/2008; the shareholder freely fixes the subscribed capital. Paid-up contributions in cash must be fully disbursed within two years from registration; no escrow account is legally required. The registered capital must be paid in full before any subsequent capital increase is registered.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] S.A.S. — Adopted in Bogotá D.C. pursuant to Law 1258 of 2008 and the Articles of Incorporation. 1. The sole shareholder hereby accepts the full subscription of the authorized capital and acknowledges receipt of paid-up contributions. 2. The registered office is adopted at the address filed in the incorporation document; any change shall require an amendment. 3. The officers are appointed: [Name] as Legal Representative and [Name] as alternate representative, each with the powers granted by Law 1258/2008. 4. The Legal Representative is instructed to execute the commercial registration before the Chamber of Commerce, obtain the RUT from DIAN, and open the corporate bank account. 5. This resolution is effective immediately and shall be filed with the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Availability Verification (Certificado de Homonimia)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá — online window (www.ccb.org.co) or in-person service desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a name-search request listing three proposed corporate names for the S.A.S. The Chamber issues a Certificado de Homonimia confirming no identical or confusingly similar name exists. The certificate remains valid for 30 days in Bogotá. The sole shareholder must verify personal identification data (cédula for Colombians; passport for non-residents) before submission.
required_dossiers: Sole shareholder's valid identification (cédula or passport)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the chosen name is rejected for similarity or phonetic equivalence, re-file the form with alternative names at no additional cost; the Chamber renders a new homonimia resolution typically within one business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Incorporation Document
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (only if real property is contributed) or private document signed before the Chamber of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Documento Privado de Constitución containing the corporate name, the specific object (3D sculpting, character rigging and game art outsourcing — ISIC 7490), subscribed capital, registered office, legal representative, and the final beneficiary declaration (Registro Final Beneficiario). If executed privately, the shareholder may sign electronically via the Chamber's 'Crea tu Empresa' portal or physically before Chamber staff; notarial authentication is mandatory only when contributions include real estate.
required_dossiers: Passport or cédula of shareholders and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For notarial observations, correct the flagged clauses and re-authenticate the signatures; for portal data mismatches, rectify the pre-validation form and resubmit the electronic filing immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration with the Chamber of Commerce and RUES
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá — Registro Público Mercantil (RPM) via RUES online platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation document, homonimia certificate, and board resolution to the Chamber's electronic counter. Pay the registration fee (derechos de inscripción) and the Notarial/Registry Tax (impuesto de registro, 0.7% of capital). The Chamber validates the shareholder identity, executes the RPM inscription, and issues the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal. This step also generates the preliminary NIT and triggers the initial ARL (occupational risk) employer registration notice.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of shareholder and legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber issues a requerimiento (query), the shareholder has up to 30 calendar days to cure the deficiency; resubmit the corrected pages or missing formalities and pay any applicable corrective fee to reactivate the registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with DIAN (NIT and RUT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) — sede electrónica and authorized Chamber of Commerce desks
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the temporary NIT obtained with the Chamber by confirming registration in DIAN's virtual office. Complete the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) with CIIU code 7490, select the ordinary corporate tax regime, and request authorization of electronic invoicing (facturación electrónica) under Resolution 165/2023. The legal representative must register with a digital certificate to sign electronic invoices and comply with foreign-taxpayer reporting obligations.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Incorporation document and First Board Resolution
Public identification numbers of shareholders and representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN rejects the form for data inconsistency, correct the RUT form via the virtual office and re-submit; if the economic activity code is queried, file Form 050 'Actualización del RUT' to amend the CIIU classification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening and Mandatory Labor-Risk Insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banks (e.g., Bancolombia, Davivienda) and Administradora de Riesgos Laborales (ARL) insurers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate checking account presenting the Certificado de Existencia, RUT/NIT and officer powers. The bank performs KYC/beneficial-owner verification. Simultaneously affiliate the company with an ARL (e.g., ARL Sura, ARL Positiva) to cover the statutory occupational risk insurance required for any physical studio staff; register the company as an employer in the social security system (Planilla PILA).
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
First Board Resolution granting banking powers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional KYC information, provide apostilled shareholder identification and the updated final beneficiary declaration; if ARL affiliation is delayed, select an alternative ARL insurer through the regulator's platform and re-run the PILA registration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — virtual/office-based creative services (ISIC 7490). For consumer and contractual matters, refer to Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating or manufacturing permit applies; the binding operating instrument is the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal issued by the Chamber of Commerce.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente y Desarrollo Sostenible / Corporación Autónoma Regional (CAR) — consult only for physical office renovation or hardware additions
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (Registration Not Required): an IT/3D-art office performs no industrial transformation and therefore does not trigger a full EIA under Decree 1076/2015 Title II; routine commercial waste rules apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater discharge; only domestic sewage to the municipal sewer network under Resolución 0631 de 2015. VOC emissions from any 3D printing equipment must remain below 50 ppm. Electronic waste (WEEE) and toners must be disposed through certified recyclers under Resolución 1512 de 2010; hazardous residues must be segregated and transmitted to an authorized gestor.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Certificado de Bomberos (fire-safety certificate) obtained from Bomberos de Bogotá every two years for the registered office; structural occupancy and load inspection per Ley 1575 de 2012; Reglamento de Higiene y Seguridad Industrial mandatory once the studio employs 5 or more workers; ARL affiliation and emergency exit protocol must be verified before physical occupancy of the 3D-art production studio.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) – National Tax and Customs Directorate; headquartered in Bogotá; principal online portal is MUISCA (Modelo Único de Ingresos, Servicios y Trámites) at https://www.dian.gov.co, with the Sede Electrónica and Carpeta Ciudadana used for taxpayer registration, e-invoice validation, tax returns, and payment proceedings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: (1) Incorporate the SAS (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada) by private written instrument filed through the Cámara de Comercio / RUES (Registro Único Empresarial y Social); no minimum statutory capital is required and 100% non-resident ownership is permitted. (2) Obtain the Matrícula Mercantil and the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal. (3) Within 30 days of incorporation, complete the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) registration through MUISCA; DIAN then assigns the NIT (9-digit tax identification number, format XXX.XXX.XXX-X) and activates the applicable tax responsibilities: CIIU 7490 activity code, IVA 'Régimen Común', income tax filer, retention-at-source agent, and information return markers. (4) Appoint a local legal representative (resident individual) and obtain the DIAN digital signature ('Firma Electrónica') from an ONAC-accredited certification authority to sign e-invoices and tax declarations. (5) Enable the Sistema de Facturación Electrónica (either DIAN's free web portal or an authorized 'Proveedor Tecnológico') and pass the initial e-invoice validation test. (6) Open a Colombian current-account bank facility for compulsory foreign-currency channeling ('canalización de divisas') and maintain the supporting exchange records (Formulario No. 5 – Declaración de Cambio) for export proceeds.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The Colombian SAS is a separate corporate taxpayer resident in Colombia by incorporation test (E.T. arts. 12, 118), taxed on worldwide net income at the standard corporate rate: 35% for FY2024 and 30% from FY2025 pursuant to Law 2277/2022. No pass-through or fiscal transparency is available to the non-resident shareholder; profits distributed abroad are subject to final dividend withholding (art. 245 E.T.) and, in applicable cases, the additional 3-point or 10-point dividend surcharge on excess distributions. Export service income is not exempt from income tax; only the VAT treatment is zero-rated.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: (a) SIMPLE – Régimen Simple de Tributación: optional consolidated income/VAT/ICA gross-receipts regime available to SAS whose shareholders are natural persons and whose annual gross income does not exceed 100,000 UVT (approx. COP 4.98 billion for 2025); service activities are taxed on a progressive scale from 1.8% to 6.8% of gross receipts; election is made at initial RUT filing or at the beginning of the fiscal year. (b) Zona Franca (Free-Trade Zone): optional authorization from the Comité de Zonas Francas for exporters of qualifying digital services, granting a 20% corporate income tax rate and 0% VAT on exports of services; entails minimum investment commitments and job creation benchmarks. (c) Economía Naranja: historically available 5-year income-tax exemption for newly incorporated SAS devoted to certified creative/cultural projects (Mincultura certification under Law 1943/2018 and Law 2010/2019), subject to quantitative caps and high compliance scrutiny. (d) No US-style 'check-the-box' election exists in Colombia; entity classification is rigid under the Código de Comercio and E.T., and hybrid mismatch rules, CFC rules, and OECD Pillar Two provisions must be observed in cross-border structuring.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto sobre las Ventas (IVA) – Colombian national value-added tax; complemented at municipal level by Industria y Comercio (ICA), which is not zero-rated by the national export regime and remains due on locally established service operations at rates of approximately 0.33%–1.14% depending on Municipality (only IVA is covered by E.T. art. 481 zero-rating).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold: a Colombian SAS performing taxable services is mandatorily categorised as IVA 'Régimen Común' from the date of its first taxable transaction, regardless of turnover. The simplified IVA regime is restricted to natural persons with prior-year gross income below 3,500 UVT (approx. COP 174.3 million for 2025) and is unavailable to an SAS. The 'Régimen Común' SAS must file monthly Form 309 (IVA returns) and, where applicable, Form 310 for export services, with payments made through DIAN's MUISCA platform.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory for all IVA taxpayers since 2021. Every sale of services, including exports, must be documented as a Factura Electrónica de Venta (FE) in XML format and submitted for real-time validation to DIAN through the authorized Sistema de Facturación Electrónica (DIAN web portal or certified Proveedor Tecnológico). Each FE must contain the CUFE or CUDS unique code, the DIAN digital stamp/QR code, the CIIU activity code, and the NIT of the issuer; transmission is generally required within 48 hours for domestic invoices, while export invoices are subject to pre-validation rules and, for services, must be transmitted within the applicable tax period before the export benefit is recognised. Late, incomplete, or non-transmitted e-invoices trigger penalties under E.T. art. 652 (1% of the invoice value) and the suspension of the e-invoicing authorization, with automatic rejection of the VAT zero-rating claim if the invoice has not been validated by DIAN.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under E.T. art. 481 and Decree 2242/2015 (as amended by Law 2010/2019), exported services are classified as 'exempt' and invoiced at 0% IVA where all of the following cumulative conditions are met: (a) the supplier is a Colombian-resident SAS registered in the RUT as an IVA Régimen Común taxpayer; (b) the recipient is a non-resident entity without domicile in Colombia (foreign AAA game studio or publishing principal) and is not a Colombian state enterprise; (c) the service is performed in Colombia but exclusively used outside Colombia, meaning the 3D sculpted assets, rigs, textures, and intellectual property are consumed, embedded, licensed, or exploited in the foreign principal's game production and not allocated to Colombian-sourced products; (d) the service is not directly connected with tangible goods located in Colombia at the time of performance; and (e) the exporter maintains contemporaneous evidence of the offshore destination, including an executed export contract, DIAN-validated Factura Electrónica de Exportación with CUFE, delivery/acceptance certificates for digital files, and inward remittance records. Digital delivery of game art by file transfer or cloud repository does not disqualify an export; however, DIAN will pierce the arrangement if the foreign client is a conduit, a related party without substance, or the final beneficiary is Colombian.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación – DEX / DEX Int.): compulsory only when physical media containing master game-art files are shipped; for pure digital transmission, the DIAN-validated Factura Electrónica de Exportación (with CUFE code) serves as the operative export document and must be referenced in the monthly Form 310.

Bill of Lading / Airway Bill (Guía Aérea o B/L): required for tangible carriers of the 3D asset packages; for digital delivery, the equivalent is the signed digital delivery or acceptance certificate (Acta de Entrega y Aceptación) from the foreign studio, including hash values or version control identifiers.

Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Canalización de Divisas / Comprobante de Compensación): issued by the Colombian commercial bank through which the foreign-currency proceeds were negotiated, evidencing SWIFT/wire-transfer receipt from the offshore client within the statutory 180-day term.

Export Service Contract (Contrato de Exportación de Servicios): executed between the Colombian SAS and the foreign game developer, identifying the parties, IP ownership and licence transfer, deliverables, milestones, payment currency, and transfer-pricing documentation consistent with E.T. arts. 260-1 et seq. (arm's length analysis for related-party clients).

Offshore-Use Certificate (Carta de Uso Exclusivo en el Exterior): signed declaration from the foreign recipient confirming that the 3D assets, rigs, and renders will be exploited solely outside Colombia and not resold, rendered, or utilised in any Colombian-domiciled game project.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN exercises a retrospective audit window of five years (E.T. art. 705) over export zero-rating claims. Where the export conditions are disproved, DIAN will assess the full 19% IVA on the exported service revenue, plus monetary moratory interest and the 'sanción por inexactitud' (100%–200% of the omitted VAT exposure) under E.T. art. 648. Additional consequences include: (i) a 1% penalty on the value of each e-invoice issued without full statutory requirements or untimely transmission (art. 652); (ii) late-filing and late-payment penalties on the reassessed VAT; (iii) fines of up to 200% of the non-canalised foreign currency under the Banco de la República foreign-exchange regime for failure to satisfy the 180-day repatriation obligation; (iv) retroactive clawback of the CUFE/CUDS validation and any previously refunded export VAT credits, with consequent recharacterisation as Colombian-source service revenue; and (v) criminal liability for aggravated tax fraud (Law 2277/2022) if fictitious contracts or inflated export proceeds are used, exposing the legal representative to imprisonment and disqualification. In practice, DIAN also applies transfer-pricing scrutiny where the foreign game studio is an affiliate, and any related-party export invoice outside the arm's length range will be adjusted with the same VAT, interest, and penalty consequences.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República (Central Bank of Colombia) acting as the national foreign-exchange regulatory authority; operational application governed by Law 9 of 1991, Decree 1068 of 2015 and Circular Reglamentaria DCIN-83, with enforcement by the Financial Superintendence of Colombia (SFC) and tax-validation oversight by DIAN.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia applies a mixed convertibility regime: current-account transactions (export service receivables, profit remittances, dividends, interest) are fully convertible with no quantitative restrictions, provided settlements flow through the official 'mercado cambiario' using an authorized intermediary (IMC). Capital-account transactions (foreign direct investment into the S.A.S., shareholder loans, equity increases and external credit) are open but must be registered with Banco de la República when the operation reaches or exceeds the regulatory threshold, generally USD 10,000 equivalent; an unregistered capital inflow makes subsequent profit and capital remittance legally unenforceable and exposes the investor to FX infringement fines. Profit remittance hurdles for the non-resident shareholder are documentary rather than exchange-control: an up-to-date FDI registration, audited or reviewed financial statements, corporate distribution minutes, evidence of payment of Colombian corporate income tax and dividend withholding tax (generally 5% for treaty-protected or low-rate jurisdictions under the 2023-2025 framework; 15% for non-residents otherwise), and processing of the exact 'Declaración de Cambio' through the IMC. There are no currency surrender restrictions on current account proceeds, but funds failing to enter the official channel are treated as a foreign-exchange offence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Colombian FX regime, 100% of export service proceeds (ISIC 7490 digital creative services) is subject to mandatory 'canalización': the exporter must collect and channel the foreign currency through an authorized intermediary and file the corresponding 'Declaración de Cambio por Exportación de Servicios'. Statutory channeling window: six months from the date of the service-export declaration, extendible by a further six months upon justified request; proceeds received earlier may be registered as advance export payments ('pago anticipado'). There is no fixed mandatory conversion ratio into Colombian pesos: the exporter may lawfully retain funds in a registered foreign-currency compensation account (Cuenta de Compensación) at a local bank or in an abroad account disclosed to Banco de la República, provided all receipts are declared in the FX market. Persistent collection outside the banking system, such as personal PayPal accumulation or foreign-currency custody without declaration, constitutes an exchange-control infringement subject to fines of up to 200% of the unreported amount.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational COP Checking Account + USD Compensation Account (Cuenta de Compensación)
Operational COP Account and Foreign Currency Account
Operational Account (Cta. Corriente) and USD/COP Treasury Products
Standard Current Account; dedicated USD account subject to branch and product availability

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: LOW-MEDIUM as a standalone primary treasury rail; MEDIUM-HIGH as a front-end collection gateway. Offshore EMIs (Payoneer, Wise, Mercury, Airwallex) are not authorized FX intermediaries under Colombian law and cannot perform the 'canalización' obligation; funds held with them sit outside the official FX market and must be repatriated to an IMC and declared for each export receivable. For the AAA game-art outsourcing commercial model, PayPal and Wise are commercially required as client-facing collection rails; the recommended structure is a tier-1 Colombian USD/COP treasury account as the principal rail, with PayPal/Wise functioning as a collection gateway swept weekly into the IMC, each sweep backed by an export declaration. Legal constraints: DIAN treats fintech balances as cash equivalents for tax accounting and demands translation into COP at the representative market rate; Banco de la República considers non-declared accumulation abroad as unreported capital; and Colombian banks may reject fintech-origin credits that lack a proper concept and invoice basis unless the client maintains an active export-registration file.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally mandatory for at least one legal representative and for the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) of the S.A.S. at the first onboarding interview; tier-1 Colombian banks require an in-branch signature protocol and personal identification under SFC AML circulars (Circular 029 de 2014 and subsequent amendments). Remote onboarding is available only for existing clients or restricted renewal cases; for a newly formed non-resident-owned S.A.S., the bank must meet the signatories in person or via an approved biometric video session, although most institutions still demand at least one physical meeting with the local legal representative. Non-resident shareholders must additionally execute a notarized and apostilled power of attorney appointing a local resident legal representative whose identity is verified in person; an alternate signatory abroad may sign under legalized power, but account structuring, FX registrations and Declaraciones de Cambio are executed by the local representative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Corporate-purpose mismatch: a single-specialty 3D art studio invoicing large amounts to foreign video-game publishers without auditable contract artifacts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master Service Agreements and Statements of Work; artifact deliverables and milestone logs; signed asset inventories; client registry with legalized foreign corporate records; and a compliance narrative describing ISIC 7490 as low-risk creative BPO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO or intermediate shareholder chain located in a non-transparent or high-risk jurisdiction, creating elevated bank exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full organizational charts down to natural persons; certified passport and residency evidence; source-of-wealth statement; bank reference letters from the UBO's home institution; external sanctions/PEP screening reports; and apostilled corporate records for each intermediate holding company.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shareholder loans or advance payments credited before service delivery, resembling migration of personal funds or unregistered external credit.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Mutuo loan agreement with defined interest and maturity; corporate resolutions approving the loan; FDI or external-debt registration with Banco de la República when applicable; source-of-funds file including bank statements and tax returns; and a forward calendar of the export contract covering the advance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recurring PayPal/EMI inflows exceeding declared export invoices or received from countries absent from the contractual client matrix.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Monthly reconciliation binder linking PayPal payout reports to the Declaraciones de Cambio; invoice-by-invoice traceability; the game-title/client matrix certified by management; and a remediation memo engaging a local AML agent to normalize prior unreconciled balances.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity and shareholder-loan injections must be sent by SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident investor's bank account directly to the S.A.S. account at the Colombian IMC, with the Remittance Information field containing: (a) full investor name and address; (b) the regulatory concept ('Foreign Direct Investment – Equity Subscription' or 'External Shareholder Loan'); (c) the S.A.S. NIT and registered name; and (d) reference to the constitutive resolutions and corporate approvals. The IMC will process Formulario No. 1 (Declaración de Cambio – Canalización) and, for amounts above USD 10,000 equivalent, will enforce foreign-investment registration (Registro Internacional de Inversiones) at Banco de la República. Where fast working capital is preferred, the client may instead receive advance payments under export contracts, a lower-compliance route requiring only a service-export declaration; alternatively, receivables can be capitalized by public deed and filed as an equity increase. Banks will block incoming funds if the SWIFT message lacks the ultimate originator (bank-to-bank information rule), if the sending institution is unlicensed, or if the routed funds show third-party consolidation; therefore all injections must carry full FATF Recommendation 16 and OFAC-validated originator data.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound treasury rails for the game-art studio consist of: (i) SWIFT MT103/M202 for payments to overseas software licensors, render-farm cloud providers and specialized subcontractors, supported by an import-of-services declaration and DIAN-certified withholding tax; (ii) MT101 batch transfers for occasional remote freelance payroll; and (iii) PayPal/Wise/Debit Rails for low-value administrative purchases below USD 2,000, aggregated into a monthly import-of-services filing. Commercial letters of credit are economically unsuitable for ISIC 7490 service flows, except where the S.A.S. acquires high-end workstations or dedicated hardware from Asian or European suppliers under documentary collections (D/P); in those cases an L/C follows UCP600 mechanics with invoice, packing list, and transport documents. Every outbound settlement must respect Colombian import-of-services withholding (up to 15% on technical services unless reduced by treaty) and the VAT output mechanism, and counterparties domiciled in grey-listed jurisdictions require a signed counterparty representation letter and enhanced KYC review before release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: COP/USD deliverable forwards with an authorized IMC, hedged against booked export receivables of 30-180 days tenor; underlying invoices and export declarations must support each position, and speculative trading is prohibited for non-financial entities.

USD/COP non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referenced to the official Colombian representative market rate (TRM), settled in US dollars for the differential, used to hedge uncertain pipeline contracts; registrable in the SFC/Banco de la República derivatives registry and subject to COP collateral rules.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) and FX swaps converting USD-denominated shareholder loans into COP obligations, permitted only when the underlying is a registered external debt instrument and with mark-to-market valuation against the TRM.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Registry Annual Renewal (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Chamber of Commerce (Cámara de Comercio) of the company's registered domicile
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before March 31, based on calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest accrues monthly; continued non-renewal leads to an administrative strike-off, prohibiting lawful operation and external contract execution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in April; exact deadline determined by the last digit of the company NIT, normally falling between April 10 and April 20
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly penalty of 5% of the outstanding tax, accumulated up to 100% of the debt; persistent failure may trigger tax lien and enforced collection, and can lead to suspension or cancellation of the tax identification number.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Owner Annual Declaration (Declaración de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Chamber of Commerce (via annual registry update) and DIAN
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than March 31, aligned with the commercial registry renewal process
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of up to 100 Colombian legal monthly minimum wages for each failing entity or administrator; failure to file prevents the commercial registry renewal and may restrict shareholder distributions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Financial Statements Filing with the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholder approval, ordinarily occurring no later than March 31 following the fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry renewal may be rejected; late filing triggers monetary fines calculated per day of delay and may impair the company's legal standing to contract with public or regulated counterparties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (Revisor Fiscal) is mandatory when total assets or gross income exceed 50,000 UVT (approximately USD 2.4 million), or when the company is a parent of a group subject to consolidation; below these thresholds, an independent certified audit may be waived but financial statements must still be prepared and filed.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Colombian Financial Reporting Standards (CNIF) based on IFRS; micro-entities may apply simplified local GAAP under Decree 2101/2016.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: All share transfers must be approved and recorded in the shareholders' meeting minutes, updated in the Board of Directors' and shareholders' register, and reported to the Chamber of Commerce within 30 days of transfer. Beneficial ownership details are reconfirmed annually through the UBO declaration filed together with the commercial registry renewal; any change in direct or indirect ownership must be filed before the registry renewal deadline.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 - 4,500 per year (if mandatory audit threshold is met)
